method_notes: WebFetch test on an apps.apple.com page (Notion, id1232780281) succeeded.
App lists came from itunes.apple.com/search. Reviews came from the itunes.apple.com customerreviews RSS JSON, page 1 only, sortBy=mostRecent, ratings 1 to 3 only.

WebFetch passes pages through a summarising model that caps quotes at about 125 characters. Quotes below are the excerpts returned in quotation marks. They are truncated, not paraphrased, but could not be checked against the raw JSON.
Reviewer names are omitted. Review dates are the feed's updated date.
Keyword volume and difficulty: no source was available to me. I did not query any. All keyword fields are empty.
Search results for 'task manager todo' and 'note taking app' were truncated at 100000 characters by the tool, so the last result of each list was not read.
Only page 1 of reviews was read per app. Counts below are complaints I recorded, not the number of such complaints in the feed.

candidates.unmet_job: Track a personal list of daily habits without a recurring subscription priced like a premium service, a habit cap, or a paywall shown before the app can be tried.

complaints.quote: $5.99 a week or $99.99 a year. Without paying one of those, you are limited to only 5 free habits.
$99/year (and not even a lifetime subscription
100 dollars a year for a habit tracker is
Cost is crazy, add lifetime and a lower fee
Paywall before you even try
complaints.note: This is the review title. The excerpt also says the tutorial cannot be skipped.

complaints.quote: limited habits, mate you post for pro but i like to break down my day step by step, get an app with unlimited habits
Why do all the apps wait to tell you you have to pay 20 bucks to use the app? Why not just buy the app?
The app updated and I no longer have lifetime access
You should not have to pay Tudor something for your mental health

trend_signals.signal: Several 2025 to 2026 reviews on Productive cite price rises, for example '$17 to $54' and '$20/year' to '$99/year'. This is reviewer-reported only.

not_found: No independent source for the price history.
candidates.evidence_strength: Pricing complaints repeat across two apps and across nine months of dates. Both apps are large, with 90K to 150K ratings. These are complaints about price, not about missing functions.

candidates.unmet_job: Keep a large personal note archive in a notes app that does not raise its price sharply, show ads or upgrade prompts when a note is opened, or restrict access to one's own notes unless a paid plan is held.

complaints.quote: they raised pricing from $69 to 129 a year, and now nearly doubling that to $249.99 a year!
I have many years of notes. I feel hostage to paying your high fees for functionality I don’t use.
Unless you want to be held hostage for your files/data and needing to upgrade to paid plan
The ads are now loud. EVERY TIME YOU TRY AND MAKE A NOTE. Unusable.
every time I open the app you force me to watch an ad before I can access my notes
Used to love this app and used it for many years until they started making things difficult
complaints.note: The summary says the reviewer found migrating away hard.

complaints.quote: forces users to pay to use Evernote across more than one device.
I expect a paid productivity application to provide reliable basic functionality.
I took all my notes here. One random update later all of my notes for every single class were missing.

trend_signals.signal: Evernote reviewers in Oct to Nov 2026 repeatedly report moving notes elsewhere and cancelling, and name Craft as an alternative in one review. Reviewer-reported only.

not_found: Price figures are reviewer-reported and unchecked against Evernote's own page.
Notion complaints are mostly about crashes and AI, so only two are used here as relevant.
candidates.evidence_strength: Strong at Evernote, with 48 low-rated reviews on page 1 across Oct and Nov 2026, most about price and ads. Notion evidence is a different problem (reliability and lost data) and is thin for this job.

candidates.unmet_job: Find a specific word or phrase inside a note, and organise notes in folders or sub-folders, in a simple notes app on iPhone.

complaints.quote: It’s almost 2027! Add folders and sub-folders to google keep and the option to change folder color (not note color).
How can you be such a big product since over 10-15 years for notes and still not have a “Search in note” feature
For years, still basic AF, no search/find function, useless and ugly interface/styles.
it will tell you which note is having a keyword but it does not highlight where the keyword lies in that specific note
Google please make this more like apple notes
Now I cannot manage my page hierarchy any more???
missing features such as nesting
complaints.note: This phrase is a summariser's wording, not a confirmed verbatim quote. Treat it as weak.

not_found: Almost all evidence is about one app (Google Keep). Apple Notes was not read because it is not a store listing with a review feed in the same form.
candidates.evidence_strength: Thin. Four Google Keep complaints across two months, one from Notion and one weak Evernote item.

candidates.unmet_job: Get task reminders that are hard to miss and fire reliably for urgent items, rather than a banner that vanishes or a push that does not arrive.

complaints.quote: Even for urgent tasks and reminders, the notification appears briefly and disappears like a regular notification,
Push notifications are broken after paying for both a personal and business plan and with recent update. Please fix!!
you get the little pop-up “added to your inbox, “ but it’s not in your inbox. It’s not anywhere this thing doesn’t work.
Not in my face enough to help

not_found: Did not read reviews for Galarm or Alarmed, so no complaints from the dedicated reminder apps.
candidates.evidence_strength: Thin. Three Todoist complaints and one from a habit app, over seven weeks. Todoist also has many crash reports in the same feed that are not about this job.
